mjm017450.issuer_capacity: Catalog metadata attributes the paper to James Madison; the page has the initials “J.M.” after the date, but no addressee or presidential capacity is stated in the visible list itself. Attribution as a Madison working memorandum is plausible; it is not a directed presidential issuance.
mjm017450.date_verified: Manuscript page ends “Aug. 10. 1814 J.M.”; matches LOC catalog date 1814-08-10.
mjm017450.original_page_matches_text: Visually examined the retained master JPEG (entire one-page list). No catalog transcription is embedded, so no text comparison possible. The manuscript visibly starts with “Wanted” and is a list of requested/past military instructions; dated and initialed at bottom.
mjm017450.operative_clause_inventory: Page reads as a checklist headed “Wanted”: apparent entries include instructions to Gen. Brown about Niagara subsequent to July 5; items concerning Brown at Sacketts Harbor; instructions concerning Detroit; matters relative to Indian negotiations by Gen. Harrison; directions for Gen. Izard; and items dated/subsequent to July 27 relating to Gen. Lewis. Some text is faint/crossed out; exact transcription is not secure. It does not set out the contents of those referenced instructions.
mjm017450.historical_inclusion_proposal: The page is an administrative retrieval checklist (“Wanted”) naming existing military instructions and commanders, not the operative instructions themselves. No separate presidential command, rule, or policy is apparent on the page; it appears to point to other instruments. This is distinct from the August 13 Armstrong signed memorandum and cannot be counted as it or as several orders.
mjm017450.possible_first_cause: Not applicable on the present instrument-identity reading; no operative order identified.
mjm017450.residuals_and_contrary_evidence: The initials/date and catalog creator support Madison authorship. The title calls it “List, Military Instructions.” It could be an internal note/request to obtain copies, which is an administrative action, but the page has no recipient, outgoing directive wording, signature, or contained operative provisions. It may be related to war instructions circulated around the same time, but not textually identical on present evidence.
unresolved_gaps: Check reverse/adjacent file context and LOC catalog record for fuller provenance.
Compare the list’s named commanders/events to actual dispatched instructions if needed to identify its administrative purpose.
No lifecycle work indicated unless separately established as an issued order.

proposal.reason: The actual page is a dated, initialed “Wanted” checklist pointing to other military instructions; it contains no independent operative order text and is not the August 13 instruction.

mjm018302.issuer_capacity: LOC metadata attributes the item to Madison and Crowninshield, but the photographed pages are headed “Instructions prepared for the Navy Dept.” and direct Captain Morris, not Crowninshield. Crowninshield was Navy Secretary at the time. The sheets themselves show no visible Madison signature; they may be a draft/prepared copy rather than a completed presidential issuance.
mjm018302.date_verified: Visible main page bears an internal date read as “1816 Oct. 16”; a top marginal annotation on that manuscript page appears “Ca. October 19, 1816,” while LOC item title/catalog dates it October 19. Date of composition versus catalog/date of letter or dispatch is unresolved.
mjm018302.original_page_matches_text: Both retained master JPEGs visually inspected. No LOC transcription is embedded. The main page (source_02; image 0495d) contains heading/date and clauses 1–5; continuation page (source_01; image 0496) contains clauses 6–8. The images have corrections/strikeouts and pale reverse-side writing; this is working manuscript text, not a clean final engrossment. Exact line-by-line transcription not made.
mjm018302.operative_clause_inventory: Main page: “Capt. Morris with the Frigate Congress” to proceed without delay to Gulf of Mexico and exercise naval command on the New Orleans station. 1 protect commerce from piracy/depredation without confusing neutral armed vessels; 2 protect commerce from unlawful armed-vessel attacks / unlawful search, with substantial strikeouts and interlineation; 3 maintain U.S. territorial rights within acknowledged limits while respecting friendly foreign powers; 4 aid according to law in suppressing smugglers; 5 prevent vessels under his command entering ports of Spanish Mexico or adjacent islands under either belligerent flag, except real emergency, and prevent unauthorized entrance. Continuation: 6 do not allow public vessels to transport/receive private property without information and proper authority; 7 do not convoy/protect foreign-flag merchant vessels; 8 communicate/cooperate as needed with U.S. land-force commander against any foreign invasion. Corrections/strikeouts materially affect clause 2 and parts of others; exact operative final reading requires transcription/edition check.
mjm018302.historical_inclusion_proposal: The content is a concrete prospective naval mission instruction to Captain Morris with eight operational clauses, not a generic private letter. However the held sheets say “prepared for the Navy Dept.,” the photographed pages lack a visible Madison signature or dispatch/receipt, and internal date differs from catalog/copy annotation. It is not yet established that this draft was issued by Madison as President. Hold for issuance/authorship/identity evidence rather than count it based on title alone.
mjm018302.possible_first_cause: Not assessed; potential mission instructions may have a bounded voyage/assignment and specific conditions, but no dispatch, effective start, completion, later continuation, or first cessation evidence reviewed.
mjm018302.residuals_and_contrary_evidence: Official metadata title says “James Madison to Benjamin W. Crowninshield” and catalog date Oct. 19. Primary pages show substantial command language and Captain Morris/USS Congress. Internal sheet heading/date says Navy Dept., 1816 Oct. 16, with ca Oct.19 annotation, and no visible presidential signature; the actual cover/dispatch may be absent. The text’s limits include exercise according to law and an exception for real emergency. Manuscript edits caution against reading every draft wording as adopted.
unresolved_gaps: Resolve handwriting/authorship and whether Madison directed or approved final text.
Locate cover letter, dispatch, Navy Department issued copy/order or subsequent correspondence showing transmission to Crowninshield/Captain Morris.
Collate crossed-out/interlineated clauses and determine final adopted text.
Clarify date of preparation vs transmission (Oct 16 vs ca Oct 19).
Determine whether this mission is within historical editorial inclusion practice (departmental/military order exclusion may matter) and whether it is separately represented in Lord/census.
Only after issuance/identity is resolved, pursue mission start/end and any later continuation.

proposal.reason: Strong operative draft instructions are visible, but the page labels them prepared for the Navy Department, lacks a visible presidential signature/dispatch, and has a date conflict and material revisions. Evidence of final presidential issuance is required before inclusion.

mjm017456.issuer_capacity: Page 1 (LOC master 0565d, rendered as local page_03) labels the document “For the Department of War”; page 2 (master 0567, local page_02) is dated “Aug. 13. 1814” and signed “James Madison.” Madison was sitting President; addressed to Secretary of War John Armstrong. Text states Secretary acts under presidential authority and subject to presidential decisions/instructions, except statutory independent powers.
mjm017456.date_verified: Verified on signed manuscript page: “Aug. 13. 1814”; workbench transcription gives the same.
mjm017456.original_page_matches_text: Visually inspected all three retained original LOC master JPEGs; opening words and structure match the embedded Hunt-edition transcription. Text is not diplomatic: manuscript contains insertions/strikethroughs and copy variants; full line-by-line collation not done. Signature and date visible on page 2; all 10 numbered topics and exception/reporting clauses visible across pages 1–2.
mjm017456.operative_clause_inventory: Intro: department normally under presidential authority/instructions, subject to statutory independent grants; routine matters may be reported after, major matters prescribed by President or preceded by sanction. Criticism of prior unapproved regimental consolidation, regulations, and a dueling order. Prospective list: 1 general/permanent War regulations; 2 courts of inquiry/martial for general officers or court membership; 3 certain commissions/appointments; 4 officer dismissals; 5 consolidations/transfers; 6 accept/refuse resignation above captain; 7 militia requisitions/receptions into U.S. service/pay; 8 Indian treaty instructions; 9 military district/corps/station movement or operations; 10 military district boundaries/separate commands/general-officer transfers. Urgent cases while President absent may waive prior communication but must be reported without delay. Military intelligence and other presidentially relevant letters immediately communicated. Closing states rules may be refined and improve interdepartmental harmony/cabinet consultation.
mjm017456.historical_inclusion_proposal: Strong evidence of a signed presidential instruction to the War Secretary that prospectively sets rules for departmental acts and requires prior communication/sanction for specified important classes. Recommend inclusion of one instrument under the project’s historical EO candidate frame, contingent on crosswalking related manuscript witnesses to this identity. This is an inclusion recommendation only; not a lifecycle conclusion or certification.
mjm017456.possible_first_cause: Not assessed. Nothing in these three pages establishes whether or when the procedural instruction was later superseded, exhausted, or ceased; Madison’s presidential term ending cannot alone supply an end.
mjm017456.residuals_and_contrary_evidence: Substantive text itself says not every act requires advance positive sanction, recognizes statutory independent powers, has emergency exception, and allows rules to be refined. Embedded transcription attributes text to Chicago Historical Society manuscripts and is edited Hunt 1900–1910 transcription converted by LOC 2001. Other LOC record mjm022917 is same date/title in Series 3 “Madison-Armstrong Correspondence” (collection description says copies of Madison letters to Armstrong), strong potential copy witness. No 022917 pages held/compared. mjm017450 Aug 10 “List, Military Instructions” may be related draft/list; no text/page available to establish if separate.
unresolved_gaps: Compare exact 017456 images and 022917 Series 3 witness pages/text; identify original sent copy versus retained copy and count as one instrument if same issue.
Check Lord/modern census crosswalk to confirm no existing identity or proxy already represents it.
Lifecycle research for first cessation and surviving effect is outside this assignment.

017450 Aug. 10 checklist was inspected and proposed for exclusion; if identity adjudication requires it, compare the named requested instructions/context to Aug. 13 instrument. The reviewed page does not itself establish a second issuance.

proposal.reason: Signed, dated, presidentially issued prospective War Department instructions with concrete operative clauses and named departmental recipient are visible in primary manuscript pages; record one instrument only pending witness crosswalk against mjm022917 and mjm017450.

No item page was held to inspect signature/copy status.
mjm022917.date_verified: LOC title/date metadata: 1814-08-13; not visually verified for this item because its pages were not retained.
mjm022917.original_page_matches_text: No item pages or transcription held; cannot compare against mjm017456. The catalog carries 8 image resources and Series 3 path mjm.27_0193_0200.
mjm022917.operative_clause_inventory: No clauses established directly from this item; potential shared text with 017456 only inferred from identical catalog title/date/addressee and Series 3 collection role.
mjm022917.historical_inclusion_proposal: Likely copy/parallel witness of the 017456 instruction; separate catalog records do not establish two instruments. Recommend duplicate/identity linkage pending text/image comparison; count one candidate if text is identical or demonstrably the same issuance.
mjm022917.residuals_and_contrary_evidence: Official collection description: Series 3 is copies of letters written by Madison to Armstrong, 1813–1814, plus some copies by others. Target item is in that series and shares title/date/addressee with 017456, which has independently inspected signed manuscript and operative text. But 022917 pages/text are absent, and exact wording, corrections, or transmission remain unverified.
